answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, non-transferable reputation token earned only by completing verified work for distinct real principals, like a marble dropped into a shared vault: the marble is locked for a cooldown and slashed if the agent misbehaves. An attacker spinning up an island of fake agents gets no nectar from the network, because stake is earned per verified job, not per account, so each fake identity must pay real work-hours and locked capital before it can transact, making mass creation unprofitable.
